correctness.rationale: At a positive endemic equilibrium, the source equations imply \(\beta S^*=\mu+\delta_1+\gamma_1+\theta_1\) and \(q=\beta I_1^*>0\). The resulting four-by-four Jacobian yields the displayed monic quartic characteristic polynomial. Exact multivariate integer-polynomial arithmetic verifies that \(A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4,\Delta_2,\Delta_3\) all expand with strictly positive coefficients in the eight positive primitive variables; \(\Delta_3\) has 331 such monomials. The quartic Routh--Hurwitz criterion therefore gives strict local asymptotic stability. The claim is explicitly limited to local stability.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2012 Guo--Li--Shuai theorem is broad for staged infection systems but the inspected statement does not establish applicability to the separate recovered-state return feedback of the 2026 SIRS equations. Röst--Tekeli 2020 proves low-stage stability for a different constant-population progression model; the 2026 authors explicitly distinguish their addition of recovery and disease-induced death at every stage. Neither source therefore dominates the present theorem as stated.

originality.rationale: The motivating 2026 article proves global stability only under additional Lyapunov inequalities and reports stable simulations outside them; it does not state or prove unconditional local stability for its two-stage model. The closest classical multistage result found is Röst--Tekeli 2020, whose always-stable result for at most three stages concerns a constant-population SIS progression system and does not contain the separate recovered compartment, waning-immunity feedback, stage-specific recovery, and disease-induced deaths of the 2026 model. Broader staged-progression global-stability literature inspected likewise does not directly instantiate this SIRS feedback system or present the present exact quartic certificate.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent theorem could exist under different model nomenclature and remain unindexed by the searches performed.

The Guo--Li--Shuai general framework was available through its authoritative abstract and bibliographic record rather than a complete theorem-by-theorem full-text applicability check, so an unnoticed specialization remains a bounded residual risk.

value.rationale: The source leaves a concrete interpretive gap: its global Lyapunov bounds are only sufficient and its simulations remain stable outside them. Proving that the endemic equilibrium is locally stable everywhere shows that any failure of global convergence outside those bounds cannot arise from an ordinary local equilibrium bifurcation in the two-stage model. This sharply separates local dynamics from the unresolved global question and prevents misreading the Lyapunov inequality as a local-stability threshold.
